math-e1-geo1.title: Names of shapes and vertices
math-e1-geo1.concept: A **triangle** has 3 sides, and a **quadrilateral** has 4. A **circle** is round and has no vertices.

math-e1-geo2.title: Exploring solid shapes
math-e1-geo2.concept: A box shape is a **rectangular prism**, a round column is a **cylinder**, and a ball shape is a **sphere**.

math-e1-l1.title: Counting numbers
math-e1-l1.concept: Count objects by pointing to them one at a time. For more than 10, it is easier to count in groups of 5 or 10.

math-e1-l2.title: Addition and subtraction
math-e1-l2.concept: **Addition (+)** combines two numbers, and **subtraction (−)** takes away a smaller amount from a larger number.

math-e1-l3.title: Comparing numbers
math-e1-l3.concept: Use **>** for the larger of two numbers and **<** for the smaller. The open side of the symbol faces the larger number.

math-e1-l4.title: Different shapes
math-e1-l4.concept: A **triangle** has 3 sides, and a **quadrilateral** has 4. A **circle** is round and has no vertices.

math-e1-l5.title: Length and clocks
math-e1-l5.concept: Measure length in **cm**. The short hand on a clock shows the hour; the long hand shows the minutes.
math-e1-l5.example: Short hand at 4, long hand at 12 → 4 o’clock

math-e2-dat1.title: Sorting and showing data in tables and graphs
math-e2-dat1.concept: Sort and count data by a criterion. Showing it in a **table** or **graph** makes comparisons easy at a glance.
math-e2-dat1.example: A: 3 people, B: 5 people, C: 2 people → 10 total

math-e2-geo1.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals
math-e2-geo1.concept: A **triangle** has 3 straight sides and 3 vertices; a **quadrilateral** has 4 straight sides and 4 vertices. Their number stays the same even when their shapes differ.

math-e2-geo2.title: Length and time
math-e2-geo2.concept: Align one end of an object with 0 on a ruler; the mark at the other end gives its length. $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. To find the minutes, multiply the number the long clock hand points to by 5.

math-e2-l1.title: Place value
math-e2-l1.concept: In a two-digit number, the left digit is the **tens place** and the right digit is the **ones place**. Ten tens make 100.

math-e2-l2.title: Adding and subtracting two-digit numbers
math-e2-l2.concept: Calculate the ones places and tens places separately. Carry when the sum is more than 10; borrow when there are not enough to subtract.

math-e2-l3.title: Introducing multiplication
math-e2-l3.concept: Repeated addition of the same number can be written more briefly as **multiplication (×)**.

math-e2-l4.title: Length and time
math-e2-l4.concept: **1 m = 100 cm**. Each time the long hand passes a number on the clock, 5 minutes have passed.

math-e2-l5.title: Finding patterns
math-e2-l5.concept: Find the **pattern** in how numbers increase or decrease to determine the next number.

math-e3-ari1.title: Adding and subtracting three-digit numbers
math-e3-ari1.concept: Calculate from the ones place onward. If a sum exceeds 10, **carry** to the next place; if there is not enough to subtract, **borrow** from the next place.

math-e3-geo1.title: Angles and right angles
math-e3-geo1.concept: A shape formed by two rays starting at the same point is an **angle**. An angle of **90°** is a **right angle**; a smaller one is **acute**, and a larger one is **obtuse**.

math-e3-geo2.title: Radius and diameter of a circle
math-e3-geo2.concept: The length from the center of a circle to a point on it is the **radius**; a line segment through the center is the **diameter**. The diameter is twice the radius.

math-e3-l1.title: Multiplication and division
math-e3-l1.concept: Multiplication is adding the same number repeatedly; **division** means splitting into equal parts. Knowing multiplication facts makes division easier.

math-e3-l2.title: Understanding fractions
math-e3-l2.concept: A **fraction** represents part of a whole divided into equal parts. The bottom number is the **denominator**, and the top number is the **numerator**.

math-e3-l3.title: Length, capacity, and weight
math-e3-l3.concept: **1 km = 1000 m**, **1 L = 1000 mL**, and **1 kg = 1000 g**. Multiply by 1000 to convert to the smaller unit.

math-e3-l4.title: Circles and angles
math-e3-l4.concept: A **right angle** is 90°. In a circle, the **diameter** is twice the **radius**.

math-e3-l5.title: Tables and graphs
math-e3-l5.concept: Organizing survey results in a table makes it easy to find the most common, least common, and total values.

math-e4-dat1.title: Reading line graphs
math-e4-dat1.concept: A **line graph** shows values that change over time using points and lines. If the line rises, the value increased; if it falls, the value decreased.
math-e4-dat1.example: From day 1 at 12 to day 3 at 20: increased by 8

math-e4-geo1.title: Angle measures in shapes
math-e4-geo1.concept: The three angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$; the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.

math-e4-geo2.title: Quadrilaterals and polygons
math-e4-geo2.concept: A **trapezoid** has one pair of opposite sides parallel; a **parallelogram** has two pairs; a **rhombus** has four equal sides. A segment joining nonadjacent vertices is a **diagonal**.

math-e4-l1.title: Large numbers
math-e4-l1.concept: Read and write large numbers using groups of ten thousand. Each digit’s value depends on its **place value**.

math-e4-l2.title: Multiplying and dividing large numbers
math-e4-l2.concept: Break the multiplier into parts, multiply, then add the results. Check division by estimating the quotient.

math-e4-l3.title: Adding and subtracting fractions and decimals
math-e4-l3.concept: For fractions with the same denominator, add or subtract the **numerators**. Align decimal points when calculating with decimals.

math-e4-l4.title: Angles and shapes
math-e4-l4.concept: The angles in a triangle add up to **180°**, and the angles in a quadrilateral add up to **360°**.

math-e4-l5.title: Bar graphs and averages
math-e4-l5.concept: Read the data to find totals and differences. The **average** is the sum of all values divided by the number of values.

math-e5-dat1.title: Finding the average
math-e5-dat1.concept: The **average** is the sum of all data values divided by the number of values.

math-e5-dat2.title: Probability
math-e5-dat2.concept: The **probability** of an event is expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). Probability = (number of favorable outcomes) ÷ (total number of outcomes).
math-e5-dat2.example: 3 balls labeled A and 2 labeled B → probability of A is $\frac{3}{5}=0.6$

math-e5-geo1.title: Perimeter and area
math-e5-geo1.concept: Rectangle: area = length × width; triangle: base × height ÷ 2; parallelogram: base × height; trapezoid: (top base + bottom base) × height ÷ 2; rhombus: diagonal × diagonal ÷ 2.

math-e5-geo2.title: Congruence and symmetry
math-e5-geo2.concept: Two shapes that have the same shape and size and fit exactly when overlapped are **congruent**. A shape that overlaps itself when folded along a line has **line symmetry**, and that line is the **line of symmetry**.
math-e5-geo2.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry

math-e5-l1.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators
math-e5-l1.concept: When denominators differ, first find a **common denominator**. The least common multiple of the denominators is a convenient choice.

math-e5-l2.title: Multiplying decimals
math-e5-l2.concept: Multiply as if the numbers were whole numbers, then place the decimal point so there are as many decimal places as in the factors combined.

math-e5-l3.title: Factors and multiples
math-e5-l3.concept: A **factor** divides a number evenly. A **multiple** is the number multiplied by 1, 2, 3, and so on.

math-e5-l4.title: Area and volume
math-e5-l4.concept: For a rectangle, area is **length × width**; for a triangle, **base × height ÷ 2**; for a rectangular prism, volume is **length × width × height**.

math-e5-l5.title: Ratios and rates
math-e5-l5.concept: A **rate** is the comparison quantity divided by the reference quantity. Multiply a rate by 100 to get a **percentage (%)**.

math-e6-ari1.title: Calculating with whole numbers
math-e6-ari1.concept: When addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division are mixed, calculate **inside parentheses** first, then **multiplication and division**, and lastly **addition and subtraction**, from left to right.

math-e6-ari2.title: Rounding up, truncating, and rounding to nearest
math-e6-ari2.concept: To **round up**, increase the target place and discard all digits to its right; to **truncate**, discard them. To **round to the nearest**, round up if the next digit is 5 or more, and down if it is 4 or less.
math-e6-ari2.example: For 3472 to the nearest hundred: round up 3500, truncate 3400, round to nearest 3500

math-e6-dat1.title: Strip graphs and pie charts
math-e6-dat1.concept: **Strip graphs** and **pie charts** show each part as a share of a whole, with the whole representing 100%. Part = total × rate.

math-e6-geo1.title: Circumference and area of a circle
math-e6-geo1.concept: Circumference = diameter × pi; area = radius × radius × pi. Pi is about $3.14$.

math-e6-geo2.title: Rectangular and cube prisms
math-e6-geo2.concept: Volume = length × width × height; surface area = 2 × (sum of the areas of three faces). A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges, and 8 vertices.

math-e6-l1.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions and decimals
math-e6-l1.concept: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and the denominators. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its **reciprocal**.

math-e6-l2.title: Proportions and proportional allocation
math-e6-l2.concept: In a proportion, **the product of the inner terms equals the product of the outer terms**. Dividing a total according to a ratio is **proportional allocation**.

math-e6-l3.title: Percentages
math-e6-l3.concept: A **percentage (%)** is a rate expressed with 100 as the reference quantity. Multiply a decimal by 100 to convert it to a percentage.

math-e6-l4.title: Circles and solid shapes
math-e6-l4.concept: A circle’s circumference is **diameter × 3.14**; its area is **radius × radius × 3.14**.

math-e6-l5.title: Mean and organizing data
math-e6-l5.concept: **Mean** is sum ÷ number of values, **median** is the middle value, and **mode** is the value that appears most often.

math-el-ai1.title: Text and image data
math-el-ai1.concept: Documents are represented as word-frequency vectors, and images as matrices of pixel values. The larger the dot product of two vectors, the more similar the documents.

math-el-ai2.title: Prediction and optimization
math-el-ai2.concept: Improve predictions using the slope of a trend line, the mean of squared errors (loss), and gradient descent $x_{new}=x-\eta f'(x)$.

math-el-cul1.title: Math in art and everyday life
math-el-cul1.concept: The golden ratio is about 1.618; a note one octave higher has twice the frequency; six Braille dots have $2^6-1=63$ possible patterns; a majority is more than half the total.

math-el-cul2.title: Math in society and the environment
math-el-cul2.concept: Use averages and rates of increase to analyze social and environmental issues mathematically. Rate of increase = (amount of increase) ÷ (initial value) × 100.

math-el-econ1.title: Interest, exchange rates, and taxes
math-el-econ1.concept: Simple interest = principal × rate × time; compound interest is principal × (1 + rate)^time. The exchange rate is the value of one unit of foreign currency, and tax is calculated by multiplying the price by a rate.

math-el-econ2.title: Supply, demand, and optimization
math-el-econ2.concept: The point where the supply and demand curves meet is equilibrium. Find maximum revenue R=pq and elasticity using functions and derivatives.

math-el-job1.title: Unit conversions and ratios
math-el-job1.concept: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g, and 1 hour = 60 minutes. Sale price = price × (1 − discount rate); when mixing in ratio a:b, A is $\frac{a}{a+b}$ of the total.

math-el-job2.title: Area, counting possibilities, and rate of increase
math-el-job2.concept: Use area to find the amount of material needed, the product rule to count possible pairs, and (amount of increase) ÷ (initial value) × 100 to find the rate of increase.
math-el-job2.example: 4 shirts and 3 pairs of pants → 12 outfits

math-el-res1.title: Ways to investigate
math-el-res1.concept: Mathematical project investigations can use methods such as literature reviews, case studies, mathematical experiments, and development research.
math-el-res1.example: Roll a die yourself to find a pattern → mathematical experiment

math-el-res2.title: Investigation steps and research ethics
math-el-res2.concept: An investigation proceeds in this order: choose a topic → plan → carry it out → present → reflect. Research ethics means citing sources and not manipulating results.
math-el-res2.example: After choosing a topic, the next step is to make an investigation plan

math-el-sta1.title: Statistical questions and samples
math-el-sta1.concept: The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of the squared deviations (the variance). Samples can be selected by simple random, stratified, cluster, or systematic sampling.

math-el-sta2.title: Estimation and hypothesis testing
math-el-sta2.concept: The margin of error for a 95% confidence interval is $1.96\times\frac{σ}{\sqrt{n} }$. If the absolute value of the test statistic $z=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu}{σ/\sqrt{n} }$ is greater than 1.96, reject the null hypothesis at the 5% significance level.

math-h1-fnc1.title: Composite and inverse functions
math-h1-fnc1.concept: The composite function $(g\circ f)(x)=g(f(x))$ is evaluated starting with the inner function. The inverse function is the function for which $f^{-1}(y)=x$ when $f(x)=y$.

math-h1-geo1.title: Shapes on the coordinate plane
math-h1-geo1.concept: The distance between two points is $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$, the midpoint is the average of their coordinates, and the slope is $\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.

math-h1-geo2.title: Equation of a Circle
math-h1-geo2.concept: Equation of circle with centre $(a, b)$ and radius $r$ na $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$. Distance between point $(x_0,y_0)$ and line $ax+by+c=0$ na $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2} }$.

math-h1-l1.title: Polynomial Division and Remainder Theorem
math-h1-l1.concept: When you divide $P(x)$ by $x-a$, di remainder na $P(a)$. If $P(a)=0$, then $x-a$ na a factor.

math-h1-l2.title: Complex Numbers and the Quadratic Discriminant
math-h1-l2.concept: $i^2=-1$. If discriminant $D=b^2-4ac<0$, di equation get complex roots. For a quadratic equation with real coefficients, complex roots come in conjugate pairs.

math-h1-l3.title: Quadratic Inequalities
math-h1-l3.concept: Use where di graph of quadratic function dey compared to $x$-axis to find di solution. $(x-a)(x-b)<0$ means between di two roots; $>0$ means outside dem.

math-h1-l4.title: Permutations and Combinations
math-h1-l4.concept: If order matter, use permutation $_nP_r$; if e no matter, use combination $_nC_r$. To solve “at least one”, subtract di complement event from di total.

math-h1-l5.title: Equations of Lines and Circles
math-h1-l5.concept: Distance between a point and a line na $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2} }$; circle equation na $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$; tangent dey perpendicular to radius.
math-h1-l5.example: At point $(3,\ 4)$ on circle $x^2+y^2=25$, slope of tangent $=-\frac34$

math-h1-mat1.title: Meaning and Operations of Matrices
math-h1-mat1.concept: **Matrix** na numbers wey arrange inside rectangular shape. For addition, subtraction, and multiplication by a real number, calculate matching entries. Di (i, j) entry of product $AB$ na sum of products of matching entries from row i of $A$ and column j of $B$.

math-h1-pol1.title: Factoring and Cubic or Quartic Equations
math-h1-pol1.concept: Use synthetic division or substitution to **factor** cubic and quartic equations, then solve by finding values wey make each factor equal 0. Use discriminant to check whether a quadratic factor get real roots.

math-h1-set1.title: Sets and Propositions
math-h1-set1.concept: $n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)$, and a set with n elements get $2^n$ subsets. The contrapositive of “if p, then q” get di same truth value as di original statement, but di converse no always get di same truth value.

math-h2-geo1.title: Triangles and Trigonometric Functions
math-h2-geo1.concept: Sine rule: $\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R$; cosine rule: $c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$; area of triangle: $\frac12ab\sin C$.

math-h2-geo2.title: Radians and Sectors
math-h2-geo2.concept: $180^\circ=\pi$ radians. For sector with radius $r$ and central angle $\theta$ (in radians), arc length na $r\theta$ and area na $\frac12r^2\theta$.

math-h2-l1.title: Exponents and Logarithms
math-h2-l1.concept: $\log_a b=x \iff a^x=b$. Sum of logarithms means multiply di numbers inside; difference means divide dem. Exponential growth fit be written as $a\cdot r^t$.

math-h2-l2.title: Trigonometric functions
math-h2-l2.concept: $\pi$ radians $=180^\circ$. Signs of $\sin,\ \cos,\ \tan$ change in each quadrant. For $y=a\sin bx+c$, maximum value na $|a|+c$, and period na $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$.

math-h2-l3.title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences
math-h2-l3.concept: $a_n=a+(n-1)d$, $a_n=ar^{n-1}$. Sum of an arithmetic sequence na $S_n=\frac{n(a+l)}{2}$.

math-h2-l4.title: Limits and continuity of functions
math-h2-l4.concept: For a $\frac00$ form, factor and cancel. As $x\to\infty$, divide by the highest power. For continuity, left limit, right limit, and function value must all be equal.

math-h2-l5.title: Differentiation and its uses
math-h2-l5.concept: $(x^n)'=nx^{n-1}$. $f'(a)$ na slope of tangent, and sign of $f'$ tell you where function increase or decrease and where local maxima or minima dey. Velocity na derivative of position.

math-h2-seq1.title: Sequence sums and ∑
math-h2-seq1.concept: $\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k$ mean $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n$. $\sum k=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, $\sum c=cn$, and $\sum(a_k+b_k)=\sum a_k+\sum b_k$.

math-h3-cal1.title: Differentiating different functions
math-h3-cal1.concept: For a composite function, differentiate the outer function and multiply by derivative of inner function. For a quotient, use $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$. Also, $(e^x)'=e^x$, $(\ln x)'=\frac{1}{x}$, $(\sin x)'=\cos x$, $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$.

math-h3-cnt1.title: Permutations and combinations with repetition, and binomial theorem
math-h3-cnt1.concept: For **permutations with repetition**, arrange items in a row by multiplying (number of choices) by itself (number of positions) times. For permutations with identical items, divide factorial of all items by factorials of identical groups. **Combinations with repetition**: $_nH_r={}_{n+r-1}C_r$. Coefficient of $x^k$ in $(x+1)^n$ na $_nC_k$.
math-h3-cnt1.example: Number of ways to arrange aabbc na $5!\div(2!\times2!)=30$.

math-h3-geo1.title: Conic sections
math-h3-geo1.concept: Focus of parabola $y^2=4px$ na $(p,0)$. For ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $c^2=a^2-b^2$; for hyperbola, $c^2=a^2+b^2$.

math-h3-geo2.title: Plane vectors
math-h3-geo2.concept: Magnitude of vector $(x,y)$ na $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; dot product na $x_1x_2+y_1y_2$. If two vectors dey perpendicular, their dot product na 0.

math-h3-l1.title: Indefinite and definite integrals
math-h3-l1.concept: $\int x^n dx=\frac{x^{n+1} }{n+1}+C$, $\int_a^b f(x)dx=F(b)-F(a)$. Swapping upper and lower limits change di sign; you fit split an interval.

math-h3-l2.title: Uses of definite integrals
math-h3-l2.concept: Integrate $|f(x)|$ to find area. Split off parts where graph dey below $x$-axis. Between two curves, integrate (upper)−(lower). Integral of velocity gives distance travelled.

math-h3-l3.title: Geometric series
math-h3-l3.concept: If $|r|<1$, series $\sum ar^{n-1}=\frac{a}{1-r}$ converge. If $|r|\ge 1$, e diverge. You fit use am for recurring decimals and repeated motion.

math-h3-l4.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
math-h3-l4.concept: $P(B\mid A)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A)}$. If events dey independent, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$, and probability for independent trials na $_nC_k\,p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$.

math-h3-l5.title: Binomial and Normal Distributions
math-h3-l5.concept: For $B(n,p)$, mean na $np$ and variance na $np(1-p)$. Standardize normal distribution with $Z=\frac{X-m}{\sigma}$; e dey symmetrical around di mean.

math-h3-pro1.title: Addition Rule of Probability and Complement Events
math-h3-pro1.concept: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$. Probability of di complement event na $P(A^c)=1-P(A)$.

math-l1.title: Finding di Value of an Expression
math-l1.concept: Putting a number in place of a letter is called **substitution**. Di result after substitution and calculation na **di value of di expression**. When you put in a negative number, use brackets to avoid mistake.

math-l2.title: Properties of Equations
math-l2.concept: An equation be like a **balance scale**. If you add or subtract di same number on both sides, or multiply or divide both sides (by a number wey no be 0), di scale still balance.
math-l2.example: If you subtract $5$ from both sides of $x+5=9$, you get $x=4$.

math-l3.title: Solving Linear Equations
math-l3.concept: Move all terms wey get $x$ to one side, and numbers to di other side. When you move a term across, change its sign. Last, divide by di number in front of $x$.

math-l4.title: Solving Word Problems with Equations
math-l4.concept: For word problems, first **let $x$ stand for what you want to find**, then turn di words into an equation, solve am, and check if di answer satisfy di conditions.
math-l4.example: Three times a number plus 2 equals 14 → $3x+2=14$ → $x=4$

math-m1-crd1.title: Coordinate Plane
math-m1-crd1.concept: Show di position of a point as (x-coordinate, y-coordinate). Di signs of di coordinates show which of quadrants 1 to 4 di point dey. Reflection across di x-axis changes di sign of di y-coordinate.

math-m1-fac1.title: Prime Factorization, Greatest Common Divisor, and Least Common Multiple
math-m1-fac1.concept: Writing a natural number as a product of prime numbers na **prime factorization**. Di biggest common divisor na **greatest common divisor**, and di smallest common multiple na **least common multiple**.

math-m1-geo1.title: Angles and Polygons
math-m1-geo1.concept: Vertically opposite angles are equal, and corresponding and alternate angles between parallel lines are equal. Sum of interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon na $180^\circ\times(n-2)$.

math-m1-geo2.title: Measuring Sectors and 3D Shapes
math-m1-geo2.concept: Arc length $=2\pi r\times\frac{a}{360}$, sector area $=\pi r^2\times\frac{a}{360}$, sphere volume $=\frac43\pi r^3$, and cone volume $=\frac13\pi r^2h$.

math-m1-neg1.title: Calculating with Integers and Rational Numbers
math-m1-neg1.concept: When you add two numbers with di same sign, add their absolute values. If their signs differ, subtract di smaller absolute value from di bigger one, and use di sign of di bigger one. For multiplication and division, same signs give +, different signs give −.

math-m1-prp1.title: Direct and Inverse Proportion
math-m1-prp1.concept: **Direct proportion** get form y=ax; **inverse proportion** get form $y=\frac{a}{x}$. For direct proportion, y÷x stay constant; for inverse proportion, x×y stay constant.
math-m1-prp1.example: Direct proportion where y=6 when x=2: y=3x.

math-m1-sta1.title: Measures of Central Tendency and Relative Frequency
math-m1-sta1.concept: **Median** na middle value when numbers dey arranged by size; **mode** na value wey appear most. **Relative frequency** = (frequency) ÷ (total frequency).

math-m2-geo1.title: Properties of Triangles and Quadrilaterals
math-m2-geo1.concept: Two base angles of isosceles triangle equal. For parallelogram, two neighboring angles add up to $180^\circ$, and line segment joining midpoints of two sides of triangle na half of third side.

math-m2-geo2.title: Similarity and Pythagorean Theorem
math-m2-geo2.concept: Similar shapes get equal ratios for corresponding sides, and area ratio na square of similarity ratio. For right triangle, $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

math-m2-l1.title: Exponent Rules and Polynomials
math-m2-l1.concept: When multiplying powers with same base, add exponents; power raised to another power, multiply exponents. For polynomial, group like terms and calculate.

math-m2-l2.title: Systems of Linear Equations
math-m2-l2.concept: Remove one variable from two equations to find solution. Choose elimination or substitution method based on situation.

math-m2-l3.title: Linear Inequalities
math-m2-l3.concept: Solve similar to equations, but when you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse inequality sign.

math-m2-l4.title: Linear Functions and Graphs
math-m2-l4.concept: For $y=ax+b$, a na slope and b na y-intercept. Parallel lines get same slope.

math-m2-l5.title: Counting and Probability
math-m2-l5.concept: Probability = (number of outcomes wey happen) ÷ (number of all outcomes). For independent events wey happen together, multiply probabilities; for “at least”, use complement event.

math-m2-lfn1.title: Linear Functions and Linear Equations
math-m2-lfn1.concept: For linear function y=ax+b, a na slope and b na y-intercept. Intersection of two graphs na solution to system of two equations.

math-m2-rec1.title: Repeating Decimals
math-m2-rec1.concept: A decimal wey same digits continue repeating after decimal point na **repeating decimal**; repeated part na **repetend**. If denominator of simplified fraction contains only 2 or 5 as prime factors, decimal terminates.

math-m3-geo1.title: Trigonometric Ratios
math-m3-geo1.concept: For right triangle, $\sin A$ = (height) ÷ (hypotenuse), $\cos A$ = (base) ÷ (hypotenuse), and $\tan A$ = (height) ÷ (base).

math-m3-geo2.title: Properties of Circles
math-m3-geo2.concept: Inscribed angle subtending an arc na half of central angle. Tangent perpendicular to radius, and opposite angles of quadrilateral inscribed in circle add up to $180^\circ$.

math-m3-l1.title: Square Roots and Real Numbers
math-m3-l1.concept: $\sqrt{a}$ na non-negative number wey square to give $a$. Take square factors outside radical, and rationalize denominator if e get radical.

math-m3-l2.title: Expansion Identities and Factorization
math-m3-l2.concept: $(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$, $(a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2$. Factorization na reverse use of expansion identities.

math-m3-l3.title: Quadratic Equations
math-m3-l3.concept: Make equation look like $AB=0$ using factorization. Discriminant $D=b^2-4ac$ show how many roots there be; relationship between roots and coefficients fit also help.

math-m3-l4.title: Quadratic Functions and Graphs
math-m3-l4.concept: Vertex of $y=a(x-p)^2+q$ na $(p,\ q)$, and sign of a determine curve direction. Change to completed-square form to find vertex.

math-m3-l5.title: Trigonometric Ratios
math-m3-l5.concept: For right-angled triangle, $\sin A=\frac{\text{opposite side} }{\text{hypotenuse} }$, $\cos A=\frac{\text{adjacent side} }{\text{hypotenuse} }$, and $\tan A=\frac{\text{opposite side} }{\text{adjacent side} }$.

math-m3-sta1.title: Variance and Standard Deviation
math-m3-sta1.concept: **Deviation**=(data value)−(mean). **Variance** na the average of squared deviations, and **standard deviation** na the positive square root of the variance. The bigger the value, the more spread out the data dey from the mean.

m-h3-cond-1.prompt: For events $A,\ B$, if $P(A)=0.5$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.2$, what is $P(B\mid A)$? (Write a decimal, for example 0.25.)
hints: Conditional probability is $P(B\mid A)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A)}$.

m-h3-cond-2.prompt: A bag has 3 white balls and 2 black balls. You draw one ball twice without replacement. What is the probability that both balls are white? (Write a decimal, for example 0.25.)
hints: Multiply the probability the first ball is white by the probability the second is white given the first was white.
$\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{2}{4}$

m-h3-cond-3.prompt: If $P(A)=0.4$, $P(B)=0.5$, and $P(A\cap B)=0.2$, then events $A,\ B$ are independent.
m-h3-cond-3.explanation: $0.4\times 0.5=0.2$, which equals $P(A\cap B)=0.2$, so the events are independent.
hints: If events are independent, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$.
Calculate $0.4\times 0.5$ and compare it with $P(A\cap B)$.

m-h3-cond-4.prompt: Of a product batch, 60% are made at Factory A and 40% at Factory B. The defect rates are 2% at A and 3% at B. If a randomly chosen product is defective, what is the probability it came from Factory A? (Write a decimal, for example 0.25.)
hints: Calculate (defective products from A) ÷ (all defective products).
Defective from A: $0.6\times 0.02$; from B: $0.4\times 0.03$.

m-h3-norm-1.prompt: If random variable $X$ dey follow binomial distribution $B(20,\ 0.3)$, wetin be $E(X)$? (Write numbers only)

ai_convolve.prompt: Apply filter $K={ker}$ to image $I={img}$, moving it one cell at a time. At each position, multiply overlapping values and add dem all together to build matrix (feature map). hints: First check argument condition (argument must be positive).
If base less than $1$, reverse inequality sign when you remove logarithm.
alg_logInequality.explanation: Since ${work}$, there are ${ans}$ integer values of $x$.

alg_obtuseCount.prompt: How many natural numbers x make an obtuse triangle possible when side lengths be ${a}$, ${b}$, and $x$? (Write number only)
hints: For three sides make triangle, longest side must be shorter than sum of other two.
For obtuse triangle, square of longest side must be greater than sum of squares of other sides. Split cases: x is longest, or side ${b}$ is longest.
alg_obtuseCount.explanation: Since ${work}$, there are ${ans}$ natural number values of $x$.

alg_rationalExp.prompt: Find value of following expression: ${expr}$. (Write simplified fraction. If whole number, write whole number. Example: 3/4)
hints: Write base as a power of some number.
Use exponent rules like $(c^{q})^{\frac{p}{q}}=c^{p}$ and $(a^{m})^{n}=a^{m\times n}$. Change negative exponent with $a^{-n}=\frac{1}{a^{n}}$.

alg_realRootCount.prompt: For integer $n$ at least $2$, let $f(n)$ be number of real values $x$ satisfying $x^{n}=A$. If $A={rad}$, what be value of $f(2)+f(3)+\cdots+f({N})$? (Write number only)
hints: Consider even and odd values of $n$ separately.
Depending on sign of $A$, for even n $f(n)=2$ or 0; for odd n, $f(n)=1$.
alg_realRootCount.explanation: If $A$ positive, for even n $f(n)=2$ and for odd n $f(n)=1$. If $A$ negative, for even n $f(n)=0$ and for odd n $f(n)=1$. Count even and odd values of n to get ${work}.$$$$$$$$$$$

alg_recAffine.prompt: Given the sequence $\{a_n\}$ defined by $a_1={s}$ and $a_{n+1}={rule}$ ($n\ge1$), what is $a_{{k}}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Find $a_2$, $a_3$, $\dots$ in order.
Write the term numbers and values in a table, and apply the rule one step at a time up to $a_{{k}}$. Reduce any fractions.

alg_recAffineQ.prompt: Given the sequence $\{a_n\}$ defined by $a_1={s}$ and $a_{n+1}={rule}$ ($n\ge1$), what is $a_{{k}}$? (Enter a decimal or a fraction such as 3/4)
hints: Find $a_2$, $a_3$, $\dots$ in order.
Write the term numbers and values in a table, and apply the rule one step at a time up to $a_{{k}}$. Reduce any fractions.

alg_recParam.prompt: The sequence $\{a_n\}$ is defined by $a_1={s}$ and $a_{n+1}=pa_n+{q}$ ($n\ge1$, with positive $p$). If $a_3={t}$, what is $p$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Express $a_2$ and $a_3$ in terms of $p$.
$a_3$ becomes a quadratic expression in $p$. Choose the positive solution.

alg_rootEval.prompt: Evaluate the following. ${expr}$ (Enter a number only)
hints: Rewrite the number inside the radical as a power of some number.
Use the appropriate property: $\sqrt[n]{a}\sqrt[n]{b}=\sqrt[n]{a\times b}$, $\frac{\sqrt[n]{a}}{\sqrt[n]{b}}=\sqrt[n]{\frac{a}{b}}$, or $\sqrt[m]{\sqrt[n]{a}}=\sqrt[mn]{a}$.

alg_sectorForward.prompt: A sector has radius ${r}$ cm and central angle ${th}$. Its arc length is $a\pi$ cm and its area is $b\pi$ cm$^{2}$. What is $a+b$? (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: Convert the central angle to radians. Then arc length $l=r\theta$ and area $S=\frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta$.
First find how many times $\pi$ the angle is.

alg_sectorPerimArea.prompt: Two sectors have perimeter ${P}$ cm and area ${S}$ cm$^{2}$ (their central angles are less than $2\pi$). What is the radius, in cm, of the sector with the larger radius? (Enter a number only)
hints: If the radius is $r$ and arc length is $l$, the perimeter is $2r+l$ and the area is $\frac{1}{2}rl$.
Eliminating $l$ gives a quadratic equation in $r$.
alg_sectorPerimArea.explanation: From $2r+l={P}$ and $\frac{1}{2}rl={S}$, eliminating $l$ gives ${work}$, so the larger radius is ${ans}$ cm.

alg_seqIntTerms.prompt: The general term of the sequence $\{a_n\}$ is $a_n=\frac{{num}}{{den}}$. How many terms are integers? (Enter a number only)
hints: Divide the numerator by the denominator to rewrite $a_n=k+\frac{c}{n+r}$, where $k$ is an integer and $c$ is a constant.
Count the divisors of the constant that can be the denominator $n+r$ (for natural $n$, $n+r\ge{r1}$).

alg_seriesPattern.prompt: Find the value of the following sum. ${expr}$ (Enter a number only)
hints: Find a pattern and express the general term $a_k$ as a formula in $k$.
Calculate using formulas such as $\sum k$ and $\sum k^{2}$ (if signs alternate, group terms in pairs).

alg_sigmaSquare.prompt: For sequences $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$, given $\sum_{k=1}^{{n}}a_k^{2}={A}$, $\sum_{k=1}^{{n}}a_kb_k={B}$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{{n}}b_k^{2}={C}$, what is $\sum_{k=1}^{{n}}({comb})^{2}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Expand the square inside the parentheses.
Use the linearity of $\sum$ ($\sum(pa_k+qb_k)=p\sum a_k+q\sum b_k$) to express it using the three given sums.

alg_sigmaSubseq.prompt: The general term of sequence $\{a_n\}$ is $a_n={an}$. What is $\sum_{k=1}^{{m}}a_{{idx}}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: The expression substituted for $n$ in $a_n$ is ${idx}$. Substitute it to get an expression in $k$.
Use $\sum k=\frac{m(m+1)}{2}$, $\sum k^{2}=\frac{m(m+1)(2m+1)}{6}$, and $\sum c=cm$.

alg_sigmaTelescope.prompt: Find the following sum. ${expr}$ (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: Try expressing each term as partial fractions. For example, $\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac{1}{k}-\frac{1}{k+1}$.
When added, consecutive terms cancel, leaving only the first few and last few terms.

alg_sumToTerm.prompt: The sum of the first n terms of sequence $\{a_n\}$ is $S_n={expr}$. What is $a_{1}+a_{{k}}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: $a_1=S_1$, and for $n\ge2$, $a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$.
Do not assume that substituting $n=1$ into $a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$ gives $S_1$.

alg_survey.prompt: The distance between points A and B is ${d}$ m. From another point C, $\angle CAB=\alpha$ and $\angle CBA=\beta$, with $\sin\alpha={sa}$ and $\sin\beta={sb}$ ($\alpha$ and $\beta$ are acute). How far is C from A? (Enter a number only)
hints: Since $\angle C=180^\circ-\alpha-\beta$, $\sin C=\sin(\alpha+\beta)$.

Use $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta$, finding cosines from $\cos=\sqrt{1-\sin^{2}}$. Then use the sine rule $\frac{\overline{\mathrm{AC}}}{\sin\beta}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{AB}}}{\sin C}$.
alg_survey.explanation: ${work}$, so the distance from A to C is ${ans} m.$

alg_trigGraphParam.prompt: For function $y=a{fn}\,bx+c$ ($a>0$, $b>0$), the maximum is ${M}$, the minimum is ${m}$, and the period is ${per}$. What is the product $abc$? (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: The maximum is $a+c$, and the minimum is $-a+c$.
Use the fact that the period is $\frac{2\pi}{b}$ to find $b$.

alg_trigIdentity.prompt: For real $\theta$, given ${given}$, what is the value of ${E}$? (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$. Squaring the given equation produces a term in $\sin\theta\cos\theta$.
Square the given equation to find $\sin\theta\cos\theta$. If the expression sought contains another squared term, rewrite it using $\sin\theta\cos\theta$ as well.

alg_trigPeriod.prompt: If smallest positive period of function ${f}$ be $k\pi$, what be value of $k$? (Write simplified fraction. If whole number, write whole number. Example: 3/4)
hints: Period of $y=\sin bx$ and $y=\cos bx$ na $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$; period of $y=\tan bx$ na $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$.
Absolute value folds negative part of graph up, halving period. Rewrite squares with $\sin^{2}x=\frac{1-\cos2x}{2}$ and $\cos^{2}x=\frac{1+\cos2x}{2}$.

alg_trigPoint.prompt: Angle has initial side along positive x-axis and terminal side passing through point P$({xp}, {yp})$. If angle size na $\theta$, what be value of ${E}$? (Write simplified fraction. If whole number, write whole number. Example: 3/4)
hints: First find distance from origin O to P: $r=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}$ (if coordinates of P na $(x, y)$).
Use $\sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}$, $\cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}$, $\tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}$.

alg_trigRootCount.prompt: How many different real roots equation ${eq}$ get for $0\le\theta<2\pi$? (Write number only)
hints: Let $k\theta=\phi$, then range of $\phi$ be $0\le\phi<2k\pi$.
Count intersections of graph like $y=\sin\phi$ and horizontal line $y=$ (constant) during each period.

alg_trigSpecial.prompt: Find following value: ${expr}$. (You fit write decimal or fraction like 3/4)
hints: Change angle to equivalent angle from $0^\circ$ inclusive to $360^\circ$ exclusive.
Use $\sin30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}$, $\cos60^\circ=\frac{1}{2}$, $\tan45^\circ=1$, and sign for each quadrant.

bm_absIneq.prompt: How many integer values of $x$ from $-{N}$ to ${N}$ inclusive satisfy inequality ${ineq}$? (Write number only)
hints: First decide whether absolute value is less than or greater than a number.
If less, rewrite as $-c<A<c$. If greater, rewrite as $A<-c$ or $A>c$. Find range of x, then count integers in given range.
bm_absIneq.explanation: After removing absolute value, solutions of ${ineq}$ na ${sol}$. Among these, there are ${ans}$ integers from $-{N}$ to ${N}$ inclusive.

bm_circleLine.prompt: How many integer values of m make circle ${circ}$ and line ${line}$ meet at two different points? (Write number only)
hints: Put line equation into circle equation to get quadratic in x.
To meet at two different points, quadratic must have two distinct real roots. Use discriminant $D>0$ to find range of m, then count integers.
bm_circleLine.explanation: Substituting line equation into circle equation gives ${sub}=0$. If discriminant be D, $\frac{D}{4}={d4}$, so $D>0$ means ${cond}$. Since ${chk}$, integer m range from -${hi}$ to ${hi}$ inclusive, total ${ans}.$$$$$

bm_compUnknown.prompt: For functions $f(x)={f}$ and g, if composite function $(g\circ f)(x)={h}$, what be value of $g({k})$? (Write number only)
hints: To find $g({k})$, find x wey make $f(x)={k}$.
Put that x into composite function $(g\circ f)(x)=g(f(x))$.
bm_compUnknown.explanation: From $f(x)={k}$, $x={x0}$. Since $(g\circ f)({x0})=g(f({x0}))=g({k})$, use value of composite function ${h}$ at $x={x0}$ to get ${ans}.$

bm_countDigits.prompt: You get ${n}$ cards, each with one different digit. The digits on the cards are ${ds}$. How many even 3-digit natural numbers can you make by choosing 3 cards and putting them in a row? (The first digit cannot be 0. Write numbers only.)
hints: The units digit must be even. Choose it first, then fill the other places.
Count separately when the units digit is 0 and when it is a nonzero even digit. If a nonzero even digit is in the units place, 0 cannot be first.
bm_countDigits.explanation: When the units digit is 0: choose the remaining two places from the ${n1} cards left and arrange them, giving ${zex}. When the units digit is a nonzero even digit: choose it from the ${nz} nonzero even cards, choose the first digit from the ${n2} remaining cards except 0, then choose the middle digit from the ${n2} cards left, giving ${oex}. By the addition rule, ${z}+{o}={ans}.$

bm_discK.prompt: How many integers $k$ in $-{N}\le k\le {N}$ make the graph of the quadratic function $y={f}$ meet the $x$-axis at two different points? (Write numbers only.)
hints: For the graph to meet the $x$-axis at two different points, the quadratic equation $y=0$ must have two different real roots.
Find the range of $k$ where the discriminant $D$ is greater than 0, then count the integers in the given range.
bm_discK.explanation: For two different real roots, the discriminant must satisfy $D={D}>0$, so ${cond}$. There are ${ans}$ integers $k$ satisfying this in $-{N}\le k\le {N}$.

bm_funcCount.prompt: Set $X$ is all natural numbers up to ${m}$, and set $Y$ is all natural numbers up to ${n}$. How many functions $f$ from $X$ to $Y$ satisfy $f(1)=1$ but are not one-to-one? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Since $f(1)=1$, you can freely choose any element of $Y$ as the function value for each other element.
Calculate (all functions that meet the condition) $-$ (the one-to-one functions among them). For one-to-one functions, different inputs must get different outputs.
bm_funcCount.explanation: For functions with $f(1)=1$, each of the other ${m1} elements can take any of ${n} values, so there are ${tot} functions. Of these, ${inj}$ are one-to-one, because the other elements must take different values other than 1. So ${tot}-{inj}={ans}.

bm_ineqSystem.prompt: How many integer values of $x$ satisfy both linear inequalities ${i1}$ and ${i2}$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Solve each inequality separately first to find the range of $x$.
Show where the two ranges overlap on a number line and count the integers there. When multiplying or dividing by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.
bm_ineqSystem.explanation: Solving the first inequality gives ${s1}$, and solving the second gives ${s2}$. The integers inside the common range are ${ints}$, so there are ${ans} altogether.$

bm_lineParPerp.prompt: Line $L:{L}$ is given, and point $\mathrm{P}$ has coordinates $({x0},{y0})$. Let the $y$-intercept of the line through point $\mathrm{P}$ parallel to $L$ be $s$, and the $y$-intercept of the line through point $\mathrm{P}$ perpendicular to $L$ be $t$. What is $s+t$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The slope of a line in the form $ax+by+c=0$ is $-\frac{a}{b}$, and the product of the slopes of perpendicular lines is $-1$.
A parallel line has the same coefficients for $x$ and $y$. A perpendicular line has the form $bx-ay=k$ ($k$ is a constant). Substitute point P's coordinates to find $k.$
bm_lineParPerp.explanation: The parallel line is ${par}$. Put $x=0$ to get $s={s}$. The perpendicular line is ${perp}$. Put $x=0$ to get $t={t}$. So $s+t={ans}.$

bm_matUnknown.prompt: For matrices $A={A}$, $B={B}$, and $C={C}$, if ${ex}=C$, what is the sum $x+y$ of the real numbers $x$ and $y$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: For two matrices to be equal, entries in the same positions must be equal.
Use the entry containing $x$ to make a linear equation and solve for $x$. Do the same for $y.$
bm_matUnknown.explanation: Compare the entries containing $x$: ${eqx}$, so $x={xv}$. Compare the entries containing $y$: ${eqy}$, so $y={yv}$. Therefore, $x+y={ans}.$

bm_polyExpand.prompt: When ${expr}$ is expanded and arranged in descending powers of $x$, what is the sum of the coefficient of $x^2$ and the constant term? (Enter a number only)
hints: Expand each product separately, then combine like terms.
The identity $(ax+b)^2=a^2x^2+2abx+b^2$ may help. Keep track of the signs and coefficients in front.
bm_polyExpand.explanation: Since $({e1}){op}({e2})$, simplifying gives ${total}$. The coefficient of $x^2$ is ${c2}$ and the constant term is ${c0}$, so their sum is ${ans}.$

bm_polyFactor.prompt: The factorization of quadratic expression ${Pex}$ is $(ax+b)(cx+d)$. The integers $a,b,c,d$ satisfy $a>0$, $c>0$, $a\le c$, and if $a=c$, then $b\le d$. What is $a+b+c+d$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Consider pairs of integers that can produce constant term $bd$ and leading coefficient $ac$.
Expand a candidate and check whether its coefficient of $x$ equals $ad+bc$.

bm_propRange.prompt: For real $x$, consider conditions $p:{pc}$ and $q: m\le x\le {n}$. What is the greatest integer $m$ for which the implication $p\to q$ is true? (Enter a number only)
hints: If $p\to q$ is true, the truth set of $p$ is contained in the truth set of $q$.
First find the range of $x$ satisfying $p$. Then ensure the left endpoint of that range is at least $m$.
bm_propRange.explanation: The truth set of $p$ is $\{x\mid {lo}{rl}x{rl}{hi}\}$. For it to be contained in the truth set of $q$, $\{x\mid m\le x\le {n}\}$, we need $m\le {lo}$ and ${hi}\le {n}$. Therefore, the greatest integer $m$ is ${ans}.$

bm_quadRange.prompt: For the quadratic function $f(x)={f}$, let $M$ and $m$ be its maximum and minimum values on ${s}\le x\le {t}$. What is $M+m$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Rewrite it in the form $f(x)=a(x-p)^2+q$ to find the vertex.
The vertex’s $x$-coordinate lies in the interval. Compare the function values at the vertex and both endpoints.
bm_quadRange.explanation: Since $f(x)={vf}$, the vertex is $({h},{k})$, which lies in the interval. The endpoint values are $f({s})={fs}$ and $f({t})={ft}$, so the maximum is $M={M}$, the minimum is $m={m}$, and $M+m={ans}.$

bm_quadRoots.prompt: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the two distinct real roots of equation ${eq}$ in increasing order. What is $\beta-2\alpha$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Move all terms on the right to the left to get (quadratic expression)$=0$.
Factor to find the two roots, then substitute the smaller root for $\alpha$ and the larger for $\beta$.
bm_quadRoots.explanation: Rearranging gives ${std}=0$, which factors as ${fac}=0$. Thus $\alpha={al}$ and $\beta={be}$. Therefore, $\beta-2\alpha={ans}.$

bm_setOps.prompt: The universal set $U$ contains all natural numbers up to ${n}$. Its subsets $A$ and $B$ are the set of divisors of ${a}$ and the set of multiples of ${b}$, respectively. What is the sum of all elements of $A\cap B^{c}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: List the elements of $A$ and $B$. Consider $B$ only within $U$.
$B^{c}$ consists of elements in $U$ that are not in $B$. Select only elements of $A$ that are not in $B$.
bm_setOps.explanation: Since $A=\{{As}\}$ and $B=\{{Bs}\}$, we have $A\cap B^{c}=\{{Rs}\}$, and the sum of its elements is ${ans}.$

bm_transform.prompt: Point $\mathrm{P}$ has coordinates $({a},{b})$. Shift it ${p}$ units along the x-axis and ${q}$ units along the y-axis to get $\mathrm{Q}$. Reflect Q over the x-axis to get $\mathrm{R}$, then reflect R over line $y=x$ to get $\mathrm{S}(m,n)$. What is $2m+n$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Translation: $(x,y)\to(x+p,\,y+q)$; reflection over x-axis: $(x,y)\to(x,-y)$; reflection over line $y=x$: $(x,y)\to(y,x)$.
Find each point in order, one step at a time.

ca1_absNotDiff.prompt: For function $f(x)={fx}$, how many real numbers k make f not differentiable at $x=k$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: $|g(x)|$ has a corner where the sign of $g(x)$ changes. Check whether the sign changes at each root (whether it is a repeated root).
At a root with odd multiplicity it is not differentiable; at one with even multiplicity it is differentiable.
ca1_absNotDiff.explanation: Among the roots of the expressions inside the absolute value, ${oddr}$ have odd multiplicity and ${evenr}$ have even multiplicity. At odd-multiplicity roots, the sign changes and the one-sided derivatives differ, so it is not differentiable; at even-multiplicity roots it is differentiable. Therefore there are ${ans} such points.$

ca1_areaCubicAxis.prompt: What is the sum of the areas of the two regions enclosed by curve $y={f}$ and the x-axis? (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: Find the x-coordinates where the curve crosses the x-axis (the three roots of the cubic).
Check whether the curve is above or below the x-axis on each region. If below, reverse the sign when integrating.
ca1_areaCubicAxis.explanation: The curve crosses the x-axis at $x={rs}$. On interval $[{r1},{r2}]$, $\int y\,dx={i1}$; on interval $[{r2},{r3}]$, $\int y\,dx={i2}$. The total area is $\left|{i1}\right|+\left|{i2}\right|={ansf}.$$$

ca1_areaLineParam.prompt: The area enclosed by curve $y={cur}$ and line $y=mx$ ($0<m<{a}$) is ${S}$. What is m? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The x-coordinates of the intersections of the curve and line are 0 and ${a}-m$.
Express the integral of (curve)−(line) between the intersections in terms of m, then solve the equation where it equals ${S}.$$$
ca1_areaLineParam.explanation: The x-coordinates of the intersections are 0 and ${a}-m. The area is $\int_0^{{a}-m}\{({a}-m)x-x^2\}dx=\frac{({a}-m)^3}{6}$. This equals ${S}$, so ${a}-m={d}$ and $m={ans}.

ca1_areaParabolaLine.prompt: What is the area of the region enclosed by parabola $y={f}$ and line $y={g}$? (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: Solve the two equations together to find the intersection x-coordinates $\alpha<\beta$.
Integrate (upper function)−(lower function) from $\alpha$ to $\beta$.
ca1_areaParabolaLine.explanation: Solving the equations gives intersection x-coordinates ${al}$ and ${be}$, and the difference between the two equations is ${dif}$. Integrating (upper graph)−(lower graph) over this interval gives area ${calc}={ansf}.$$$

ca1_areaTangentParabola.prompt: What is the area enclosed by the parabola $y={f}$, the tangent at the point on it with x-coordinate ${a}$, and the y-axis? (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: First find the equation of the tangent. It lies on only one side (above or below) of the parabola.
Integrate the absolute value of (parabola)−(tangent) from $x=0$ to $x={a}$.
ca1_areaTangentParabola.explanation: The tangent equation is $y={tl}$, and the difference between parabola and tangent is ${dif}$. Integrating the absolute value of this difference from $x=0$ to $x={a}$ gives area ${calc}={ansf}.$

ca1_contProduct.prompt: For functions ${pw}$ and $g(x)={gd}$ (all letters in the expression for $g$ are constants), the product $f(x)g(x)$ is continuous for every real $x$. What is the value of $g({kq})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: At a point where $f$ is discontinuous, what must the value of $g$ be for $f(x)g(x)$ to remain continuous?
Use the condition that $g=0$ at that point to determine the constants in $g$.
ca1_contProduct.explanation: $f$ jumps at ${ptxt}$. For $f(x)g(x)$ to be continuous, $g$ must be 0 at these points. This determines the constants, giving $g(x)={gfull}$ and $g({kq})={ans}.$

ca1_contRadical.prompt: The function ${pw}$ is continuous at $x={c}$. What is the value of constant $k$? (Write a reduced fraction, or a whole number if appropriate. Example: 3/4.)
hints: For continuity at $x={c}$, the limit as $x\to {c}$ must equal $k$.
Rationalize any radicals in the numerator or denominator, then cancel common factors.
ca1_contRadical.explanation: For continuity, $k=\lim_{x\to {c}}f(x)$. Rationalizing and cancelling for $x\ne {c}$ gives $f(x)={rat}$, so the limit as $x\to {c}$ is $k={ansf}$.

ca1_contTwoJoint.prompt: The function ${pw}$ is continuous for every real $x$. For constants $a$ and $b$, what is the value of $a+b$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The possible discontinuities are where the expression changes: $x={p1}$ and $x={p2}$.
At each point, set the left and right expressions equal to make an equation.
ca1_contTwoJoint.explanation: The expressions on both sides must match at $x={p1}$ and $x={p2}$. Solving the two equations gives $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$. Therefore, $a+b={ans}.$

ca1_defIntAbs.prompt: What is the value of $\int_{{p}}^{{q}}|{g}|\,dx$? (Write a reduced fraction, or a whole number if appropriate. Example: 3/4.)
hints: Find the roots inside the interval where the expression inside the absolute value changes sign.
Split the interval at those points, remove the absolute value with the correct sign on each part, and integrate.
ca1_defIntAbs.explanation: The expression inside the absolute value changes sign at $x={zs}$, so split the interval there. Its sign is constant on each part, so add the absolute values of the definite integrals on those parts: ${parts}={ansf}.$

ca1_defIntFindBound.prompt: For positive $a$, if $\int_{{lo}}^{a}\left({g}\right)dx={V}$, what is the value of $a$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Find an antiderivative and express $\int_{{lo}}^{a}$ as a polynomial in $a$.
Find the solution with $a>{lo}$. Since the expression is increasing, there is only one solution.
ca1_defIntFindBound.explanation: One antiderivative is $G(x)={G}$, so $G(a)-G({lo})={V}$. This value increases as $a$ increases for $a>{lo}$, so there is only one solution. Solving gives $a={ans}.$

ca1_defIntSplit.prompt: For the continuous function $f(x)$, if $\int_{{a0}}^{{p}}f(x)\,dx={A}$ and $\int_{{a0}}^{{q}}f(x)\,dx={B}$, what is the value of $\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}\left({mf}\right)dx$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Use the properties $\int_a^b f\,dx+\int_b^c f\,dx=\int_a^c f\,dx$ and $\int_b^a f\,dx=-\int_a^b f\,dx$.
Express the required integral of $f$ using the two given values, and integrate the constant term separately.
ca1_defIntSplit.explanation: Over the required interval, $\int f(x)\,dx={I}$. Integrate the constant term as $\int c\,dx=c\times(\text{signed length of the interval})$ and add it. Therefore, the value is ${ans}.$

ca1_defIntSymm.prompt: What is the value of $\int_{-{a}}^{{a}}\left({g}\right)dx$? (Write a reduced fraction, or a whole number if appropriate. Example: 3/4.)
hints: The interval is symmetric about the origin. The integral of every odd-power term in $x$ is $0$.
Expand the expression, keep only the even-power terms, and calculate using $2\int_0^{a}$.
ca1_defIntSymm.explanation: After simplifying, the integrals of the odd-power terms are $0$, and the even-power terms give ${evp}$. Therefore, $2\int_0^{a}\left({evp}\right)dx={ansf}$.

ca1_derivSignMin.prompt: For the polynomial function $f$, given ${given}$, what is the sum of all values of $x$ where $f$ has a local minimum? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Local extrema occur where the sign of $f'(x)$ changes. At a repeated root (a squared factor), the sign does not change.
Check the sign of $f'(x)$ on both sides of each root. Find where it changes from $-$ to $+$.
ca1_derivSignMin.explanation: A local minimum occurs where the sign of $f'(x)$ changes from $-$ to $+$. From a sign chart, this happens when $x$ is ${mins}$, and their sum is ${ans}.$

ca1_diffLimitPoly.prompt: If $f(x)={f}$, what is the value of ${lim}$? (Write a reduced fraction, or a whole number if appropriate. Example: 3/4.)
hints: Rewrite the expression in the form of the definition of the derivative of $f$: $\lim\frac{f(a+\Delta)-f(a)}{\Delta}$. Add and subtract terms so the numerator contains $f(x)-f({a})$.
First find $f({a})$ or $f'({a})$, then combine the values to match the expression.
ca1_diffLimitPoly.explanation: First find $f'(x)$: $f'({a})={d1}$ and $f({a})={d0}$. Expressing the limit as a derivative gives ${step}={ansf}$.

ca1_diffParam.prompt: The function ${pw}$ is differentiable at $x={c}$. For constants $a$ and $b$, what is the value of $a+b$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: If a function is differentiable at $x={c}$, it is continuous there, and its left and right derivatives are equal.
Set up two equations: one for equal function values at $x={c}$ and one for equal derivative values there.
ca1_diffParam.explanation: The two function values are equal at $x={c}$ because the function is continuous, and the two derivative values are equal because it is differentiable. Solving these equations gives $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$, so $a+b={ans}$.

ca1_extremaCoef.prompt: The cubic function $f(x)={f}$ ($a$, $b$, and $c$ are constants) has a local maximum at $x={m}$ and a local minimum at $x={n}$, and $f({z})={w}$. What is the sum of the local maximum and local minimum values? (Write numbers only.)
hints: At a local maximum or minimum, $f'(x)=0$. Use $f'({m})=f'({n})=0$ to find $a$ and $b$.
After finding $a$ and $b$, use the condition $f({z})={w}$ to find $c$. Finally, calculate and add the local maximum $f({m})$ and local minimum $f({n})$.
ca1_extremaCoef.explanation: From $f'({m})=f'({n})=0$, we get $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$. From $f({z})={w}$, we get $c={cv}$. The local maximum is $f({m})={fm}$ and the local minimum is $f({n})={fn}$, so their sum is ${ans}.$

ca1_indefInitial.prompt: The derivative of the function $f(x)$ is $f'(x)={d}$, and $f({p})={q}$. What is the value of $f({r})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: $f(x)$ is an indefinite integral of $f'(x)$. Find $f(x)$, including the integration constant $C$.
Use the condition $f({p})={q}$ to find the integration constant $C$, then find $f({r})$.

ca1_indefSecond.prompt: For the function $f(x)$, $f''(x)={d}$, $f'({p})={s}$, and $f({q})={w}$. What is the value of $f({r})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Integrate $f''$ once to get $f'$, and once more to get $f$. Each integration adds an integration constant.
Use $f'({p})={s}$ to find the first constant, then $f({q})={w}$ to find the second constant.
ca1_indefSecond.explanation: Integrate $f''$ and use $f'({p})={s}$ to find the constant; this gives $f'(x)={g1}$. Integrate again and use $f({q})={w}$ to find the next constant; this gives $f(x)={g0}$. Therefore $f({r})={ans}.$

ca1_ineqParam.prompt: For the function $f(x)={f}$ on the interval ${dom}$, what is the minimum real value of $a$ such that $f(x)+a\ge 0$ always holds? (Write numbers only.)
hints: For $f(x)+a\ge0$ to always hold, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval must be at least $-a$.
Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval by comparing its local extrema with the function values at the interval endpoints.
ca1_ineqParam.explanation: The minimum value of $f(x)$ on this interval is ${mn}$. For $f(x)+a\ge0$ to always hold, $a\ge {mn2}$, so the minimum value of $a$ is ${ans}.$

ca1_integralEq.prompt: For a polynomial $f(x)$, suppose $f(x)={rhs}$ for all real $x$. What is $f({k})$? (Enter a number only)
hints: $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt$ is a constant independent of $x$. Let it be $c$, then express $f(x)$ in terms of $c$.
Substitute that expression into $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt=c$ and solve for $c$.
ca1_integralEq.explanation: Let $\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt=c$ (a constant). Then $f(x)$ is a quadratic expression involving $c$. Setting its integral from 0 to 1 equal to $c$ gives $c={c}$, and $f({k})={ans}.$

ca1_integralFuncExtremum.prompt: Given $f(t)={f}$, what is the local minimum value of $G(x)=\int_{{s}}^{x}f(t)\,dt$? (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: Since $G'(x)=f(x)$, the sign of $f(x)$ determines whether $G$ is increasing or decreasing.
G has a local minimum where the sign of $f(x)$ changes from $-$ to $+$. Find its value using $\int_{{s}}^{x}f(t)\,dt$.
ca1_integralFuncExtremum.explanation: The sign of $G'(x)=f(x)$ changes from $-$ to $+$ at $x={z}$. The local minimum is $G({z})=\int_{{s}}^{{z}}f(t)\,dt={ansf}.$

ca1_integralFuncFind.prompt: A polynomial $f(x)$ satisfies $\int_{{c}}^{x}f(t)\,dt={F}$ for all real $x$ ($a$ is a constant). Find $f({k})$. (Enter a number only)
hints: At $x={c}$, the integral on the left is $0$, which lets you find $a$.
Then differentiate both sides with respect to $x$ to get $f(x)$.
ca1_integralFuncFind.explanation: At $x={c}$, the left side is $0$, so $a={av}$. Differentiating both sides gives $f(x)={fx}$, hence $f({k})={ans}.$

ca1_integralLimit.prompt: For the polynomial $f(x)={f}$, find ${lim}$. (Write a simplified fraction, or an integer if it is whole; e.g. 3/4)
hints: Both numerator and denominator approach $0$. Use $\frac{d}{d x}\int_a^x f(t)\,dt=f(x)$, the relation between definite and indefinite integrals.
If $F'(x)=f(x)$, write $\int_a^x f(t)\,dt=F(x)-F(a)$ to get the definition of a derivative.
ca1_integralLimit.explanation: Writing the integral as $F(\text{upper limit})-F(\text{lower limit})$, where $F'(x)=f(x)$, puts the limit in the form of a derivative of $F$. Its value is ${step}={ansf}.$

ca1_ivtCount.prompt: How many integer values of $a$ make the equation ${fx}=0$ have a real root in the open interval $({m},{n})$? (Enter a number only)
hints: This function is increasing throughout the interval. Therefore, its values at the two endpoints must have opposite signs.
Write the condition that $f({m})$ and $f({n})$ have opposite signs, namely $f({m})f({n})<0$, as an inequality in $a$.
ca1_ivtCount.explanation: Since $f(x)={fx}$ has $f'(x)>0$, it is increasing. The necessary and sufficient condition for a root in the interval is $f({m})f({n})<0$. The integer values of $a$ satisfying this are ${alo}<a<{ahi}$, so there are ${ans}.$

ca1_kinCoefFind.prompt: A point P moves on a number line with position $x(t)={f}$ at time $t$ ($a$ and $b$ are constants). At time $t={p}$, its velocity is 0 and its acceleration is ${q}$. What is its position at time $t={k}$? (Enter a number only)
hints: Velocity is $v(t)=x'(t)$ and acceleration is $a(t)=v'(t)$. Write the two conditions as $v({p})=0$ and $a({p})={q}$.
Solve the two equations for $a$ and $b$, then calculate $x({k})$.
ca1_kinCoefFind.explanation: Since $v(t)=x'(t)$ and $a(t)=x''(t)$, the conditions $v({p})=0$ and $a({p})={q}$ give $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$. Therefore, $x({k})={ans}.$

ca1_limCoefPoly.prompt: For function $f(x)={f}$ (where $a$, $b$ be constants), if ${lim}={L}$, what be value of $f(1)$? (Write number only)
hints: Limit dey exist and denominator become $0$, so numerator also suppose become $0$ at $x={c}$.
Then limit na ${rel}$. Use equation say dis equal ${L}$, together with numerator condition, to form simultaneous equations for $a$ and $b$.
ca1_limCoefPoly.explanation: Since numerator suppose be $0$ at $x={c}$, $f({c})={m0}$. Limit na ${rel}$ and e equal ${L}$. Solve both equations together to get $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$, then $f(1)={ans}.$

ca1_limCoefRational.prompt: If $\lim_{x\to {c}}\frac{{num}}{{den}}={L}$, what be value of $a+b$ for constants $a$ and $b$? (Write number only)
hints: For limit to exist at $x={c}$ where denominator become $0$, numerator also suppose become $0$.
Express $b$ in terms of $a$ so numerator get factor ${xc}$. Then set limit of simplified expression equal to given value (${L}$).
ca1_limCoefRational.explanation: Since limit dey exist and denominator become $0$ at $x={c}$, numerator also suppose become $0$. Cancel common factor in numerator and denominator. Set resulting limit equal to given value (${L}$) to get $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$. Therefore $a+b={ans}.$$$

ca1_limDerivForm.prompt: For differentiable function $f(x)$, if $f({a})={s}$ and $f\prime({a})={t}$, what be value of ${lim}$? (Write simplified fraction. If whole number, write whole number. Example: 3/4)
hints: Add and subtract or factorize so numerator show form $f(x)-f({a})$ (or $f(a+h)-f(a)$).
Definition of derivative: $\lim_{x\to {a}}\frac{f(x)-f({a})}{{xa}}=f\prime({a})$.
ca1_limDerivForm.explanation: Make numerator look like $f(x)-f({a})$ and use definition of derivative. Since $f({a})={s}$ and $f\prime({a})={t}$, limit na ${step}={ansf}.$

ca1_limExistence.prompt: For function ${pw}$, if value of $\lim_{x\to {c}}f(x)$ exist, what be value of constant $a$? (Write number only)
hints: For limit to exist, left-hand and right-hand limits as $x\to {c}$ must equal.
Use formula for $x<{c}$ and formula for $x>{c}$ near $x={c}$ separately to express both limits with $a$.
ca1_limExistence.explanation: Left-hand limit na value of formula for $x<{c}$ as $x\to {c}$; right-hand limit na value of formula for $x>{c}$. Since dem must equal, $a={ans}.$

ca1_limInfRatio.prompt: Wetin be value of $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{{num}}{{den}}$? (Write simplified fraction. If whole number, write whole number. Example: 3/4)
hints: First compare highest powers in numerator and denominator. If numerator degree lower, limit na $0$.
Divide numerator and denominator by biggest power of $x$.
ca1_limInfRatio.explanation: As $x\to\infty$, numerator behavior determined by ${nl}$ and denominator by ${dl}$. So limit equal limit of ratio $\frac{{nl}}{{dl}}$, and answer na ${ansf}.$

ca1_limPiecewise.prompt: For function ${pw}$, what be value of {ask}? (Write number only)
hints: Formula for function $f$ change at $x={k}$. First decide whether input inside $f$ dey approach ${k}$ from below or above.
Use formula for correct side and find value when $x={k}$. Function value $f({k})$ no affect limit.
ca1_limPiecewise.explanation: When $x\to {k}^{-}$, limit na ${lv}$; when $x\to {k}^{+}$, na ${rv}$. (Function value at $x={k}$ na ${e}$, but e no affect limit.) Check which side di inside value approach ${k}$ for di requested expression, use right values, and answer na ${ans}.$

ca1_limRadical.prompt: What is the value of $\lim_{x\to\infty}\left({expr}\right)$? (You can write a decimal or a fraction like 3/4.)
hints: To simplify a difference of expressions with radicals, or a radical expression and a linear expression, multiply the numerator and denominator by their conjugate expression.
After rationalizing, divide the numerator and denominator by $x$ and let $x\to\infty$.
ca1_limRadical.explanation: Rationalizing the numerator changes the expression to the form $\frac{{numr}}{{den2}}$. After dividing the numerator and denominator by $x$, the numerator approaches ${nc}$ and the denominator approaches ${dc}$, so the limit is ${ans}.$

ca1_maxMinFind.prompt: The maximum value of the function $f(x)={f}$ ($a$ is a constant) on the closed interval $[{s},{t}]$ is ${M}$. What is its minimum value on this interval? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Find the maximum and minimum on a closed interval by comparing the extrema inside the interval with the function values at both endpoints.
Find the maximum while keeping $a$ in the expression to determine $a$, then use the same method to find the minimum.
ca1_maxMinFind.explanation: Comparing the extrema inside the interval with the endpoint values gives the maximum ${mx0}+a$. Since this equals ${M}$, $a={av}$. The minimum is ${mn0}+a={ans}.$

ca1_monoGiven.prompt: The cubic function $f(x)={f}$ ($a$ and $b$ are constants) decreases on the closed interval $[{m},{n}]$ and increases on each of the intervals $(-\infty,{m}]$ and $[{n},\infty)$. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum values of $f(x)$ on $[{m},{n}]$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: At $x={m}$ and $x={n}$, where $f$ changes from increasing to decreasing and from decreasing to increasing, $f'(x)=0$.

Since $f'(x)$ is a quadratic with roots $x={m}$ and $x={n}$, write it in the form (coefficient of the quadratic term)\times{fm}{fn} and find $a$ and $b$. On a decreasing interval, at which endpoint do the maximum and minimum occur?
ca1_monoGiven.explanation: Since the increase/decrease changes at $x={m}$ and $x={n}$, $f'(x)=0$ there, so $f'(x)={d3}{fm}{fn}$. Comparing coefficients gives $a={av}$ and $b={bv}$. As the function decreases on the interval, the maximum is $f({m})={fmv}$ and the minimum is $f({n})={fnv}$. Their difference is ${ans}.$

ca1_mvtBound.prompt: A differentiable function $f(x)$ satisfies ${lo}\le f'(x)\le {hi}$ for all real $x$, and ${cond}$. What is the maximum value of $f({b})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: By the mean value theorem, there is a $c$ such that $f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a)$. Use the maximum possible value of $f'(c)$.
If two points are known, use the known point closest to the point you need to find.
ca1_mvtBound.explanation: The known point closest to $f({b})$ is $x={na}$, where $f({na})={nm}$, and the gap is ${gap}$. By the mean value theorem, $f({b})-({nm})=f'(c)\times{gap}\le {hi}\times{gap}$, so $f({b})\le {ans}$. A function whose slope stays ${hi}$ can reach this value, so the maximum is ${ans}.$

ca1_mvtC.prompt: For the function $f(x)={f}$ on the interval $[{a},{b}]$, what is the value of $c$ satisfying the mean value theorem, where $c$ is greater than ${a}$ and less than ${b}$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The mean value theorem's $c$ satisfies $\frac{f({b})-f({a})}{{b}-({a})}=f'(c)$.
First find the average rate of change, then solve $f'(c)=(\text{average rate of change})$ and choose the solution inside the open interval.
ca1_mvtC.explanation: The average rate of change is $\frac{f({b})-f({a})}{{b}-({a})}={sl}$. Among the solutions to $f'(c)={sl}$, the only one in $({a},{b})$ is $c={ans}$.

ca1_noExtremum.prompt: For the cubic function $f(x)={f}$, how many integer values of $a$ make $f$ have no local extrema? (Write numbers only.)
hints: A cubic function has no local extrema when the sign of $f'(x)$ does not change.
Write the condition that the discriminant of the quadratic equation $f'(x)=0$ satisfies $D\le 0$ as an inequality in $a$, then count the integer solutions.
ca1_noExtremum.explanation: The sign of $f'(x)$ must not change, so the discriminant of $f'(x)=0$ must satisfy $D\le 0$. The integer values of $a$ satisfying this are ${lo}\le a\le {hi}$, so there are ${ans}.$

ca1_optimBox.prompt: From the four corners of a rectangular sheet measuring ${W}$ cm by ${H}$ cm, cut equal squares and fold the remaining parts to make an open-top rectangular box. What is the maximum volume in cm³? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Let x be the side length of each cut-out square, then write box volume as function $V(x)$.
The volume is largest at a solution of $V'(x)=0$ within $0<x<(\text{shorter side})\div 2$.
ca1_optimBox.explanation: Let x cm be the side of each cut-out square. Then $V(x)=x({W}-2x)({H}-2x)$ ($0<x<{hh}$). Solving $V'(x)=0$, the volume reaches a maximum where it changes from increasing to decreasing, at $x={x}$. The maximum volume is ${ans}$ cm³.

ca1_optimProfit.prompt: A business produces and sells x units per day ($0\le x\le {X}$). The total cost is $C(x)={cost}$ (10,000 won), and the selling price per unit is ${price}$ (10,000 won). What is the maximum daily profit (sales revenue minus total cost), in units of 10,000 won? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Let profit be $P(x)={price}x-C(x)$ and solve $P'(x)=0$.
Compare the profit at the local maximum and at both endpoints $x=0$ and $x={X}$.
ca1_optimProfit.explanation: $P(x)={price}x-C(x)$. The local maximum inside the interval occurs at $x={xs}$, where $P({xs})={ans}$. At the endpoints, $P(0)={p0}$ and $P({X})={pX}$, so maximum profit is ${ans}$ (10,000 won).

ca1_powerFindN.prompt: For natural number n, let $f(x)={f}$. If $f'({a})={V}$, what is n? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The derivative of $x^n$ is $nx^{n-1}$.
Write $f'(x)$ in terms of n, then consider how its value changes as n increases.
ca1_powerFindN.explanation: $f'(x)={cc}\cdot n\cdot x^{n-1}-{kk}$, so $f'({a})={cc}\cdot n\cdot{a}^{n-1}-{kk}$. This value increases as n increases, so there is only one natural number n for which the value is ${V}$, namely n={ans}.

ca1_powerTangentN.prompt: For curve $y={fx}$ (where n is a natural number at least 2), the y-intercept of the tangent at the point with x-coordinate ${a}$ is ${V}$. What is n? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Since the derivative of $x^n$ is $nx^{n-1}$, the tangent slope can be written in terms of n.
Write the y-intercept in terms of n; its absolute value increases as n increases.
ca1_powerTangentN.explanation: For $f(x)={fx}$, $f'(x)={cc}nx^{n-1}$. The tangent y-intercept is $f({a})-{a}f'({a})=(1-n)\cdot{ccp}\cdot{a}^n$. Its absolute value increases as n increases, so only one n gives ${V}$, and n={ans}.

ca1_prodAbstract.prompt: For differentiable functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, $f({a})={s}$, $f'({a})={t}$, $g({a})={u}$, and $g'({a})={w}$. If $h(x)={hx}$, what is $h'({a})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Product rule: $\{f(x)g(x)\}'=f'(x)g(x)+f(x)g'(x)$.
If the product has more than two factors, add terms where you differentiate one factor at a time.

ca1_returnTime.prompt: A point P moves on a number line, starting from the origin at time $t=0$. Its velocity at time $t$ ($t\ge0$) is $v(t)={v}$. What is its velocity when it first returns to the origin after starting? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Position is the antiderivative of velocity. Since it starts at 0, $x(t)=\int_0^t v(s)\,ds$.
Find the smallest positive t for which $x(t)=0$, then substitute it into $v(t)$.
ca1_returnTime.explanation: $x(t)=\int_0^t v(s)\,ds={xt}$, and positive t values with $x(t)=0$ are ${rs}$. At the smallest one, $t={t0}$, so $v({t0})={ans}.$$$

ca1_rootCountK.prompt: For the function $f(x)={f}$, how many integer values of $k$ make the equation $f(x)=k$ have exactly ${nr}$ distinct real roots? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Think about how many times the graph $y=f(x)$ intersects the horizontal line $y=k$.
Find the local maximum and minimum values, then determine the range of $k$ for which there are ${nr}$ intersections.
ca1_rootCountK.explanation: Find the extreme values by solving $f'(x)=0$: ${ext}$. To have exactly ${nr}$ distinct real roots, ${rng}$ must hold, so there are ${ans}$ integer values of $k$.

ca1_tangentFromPoint.prompt: What is the product of the slopes of the two tangents drawn to the curve $y={f}$ from the point $({p},{q})$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: If the x-coordinate of the point of tangency is $t$, the tangent is $y=f'(t)(x-t)+f(t)$. When $x={p}$, this line must have $y={q}$.
Use this condition to get a quadratic equation in $t$. Find its two roots, then calculate the slopes $f'(t)$.
ca1_tangentFromPoint.explanation: Let $t$ be the x-coordinate of the point of tangency. The condition that the tangent has $y={q}$ when $x={p}$ gives a quadratic equation with roots $t={t1}$ and ${t2}$. The slopes are $f'({t1})$ and $f'({t2})$, and their product is ${ans}.$

ca1_tangentIntercept.prompt: A tangent is drawn to the curve $y={f}$ at the point whose x-coordinate is ${a}$. What is the y-coordinate where the tangent meets the y-axis? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The slope of the tangent is the derivative at the point of tangency, $f'({a})$.
From the tangent equation $y-f({a})=f'({a})\{x-({a})\}$, find the value of $y$ when $x=0$.

ca1_tangentIntersect.prompt: A tangent to the curve $y={f}$ at the point with x-coordinate ${a}$ meets the curve once more, at a different point. What is the y-coordinate of that point? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The x-coordinates of intersections between the curve and tangent are the roots of (curve equation) − (tangent equation) $=0$. This equation has a repeated root at $x={a}$.
The sum of the three roots of the cubic equation can be found from the coefficient of $x^2$. Find the remaining root, then substitute it into the curve equation.
ca1_tangentIntersect.explanation: (Curve) − (tangent) $=0$ is a cubic equation with a repeated root at $x={a}$. The sum of its three roots follows from the relationship between roots and coefficients. The remaining root is $x={s}$; substituting it into the curve gives y-coordinate ${ans}.$

ca1_tangentSlopeTwo.prompt: There are two lines tangent to the curve $y={f}$ with slope ${m}$. What is the sum of their y-intercepts? (Write numbers only.)
hints: If the slope is ${m}$, the x-coordinates of the points of tangency solve $f'(x)={m}$.
At each point of tangency $(s, f(s))$, the y-intercept is $f(s)-s\cdot{m}$.
ca1_tangentSlopeTwo.explanation: Solving $f'(x)={m}$ gives ${s1}$ and ${s2}$ as the x-coordinates of the points of tangency. Find the y-intercept of each tangent and add them to get ${ans}.$

ca1_throwImpact.prompt: A ball is thrown upward from a height of ${h0}$ m above the ground. Its height after $t$ seconds is $h(t)={h}$ m. What is the speed of the ball when it hits the ground, in m/s? (Write numbers only.)
hints: The ball hits the ground at a positive value of $t$ for which $h(t)=0$. Its velocity is $h'(t)$.
Solve $h(t)=0$ to find the positive root, then find the absolute value of the velocity at that time.
ca1_throwImpact.explanation: The positive root of $h(t)=0$ is $t={T}$ seconds, and $h'(t)={v0}-10t$, so $h'({T})={vv}$. Speed is the absolute value of velocity, so the answer is ${ans}$ m/s.

ca1_totalDistPos.prompt: The position of point P on a number line at time $t$ ($t\ge0$) is $x(t)={f}$. How far does P travel from $t=0$ to $t={T}$? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Distance travelled is not just the change in position. Split the time interval whenever the direction changes, then add the distances in each part.
First check whether a time when $v(t)=x'(t)=0$ lies in the interval $(0,{T})$.
ca1_totalDistPos.explanation: Solving $v(t)=x'(t)=0$ gives the times when the direction changes in the interval: ${turns}$. Split the interval at those times and add the absolute changes in position. The total distance is ${ans}.$

ca1_totalDistVel.prompt: A point P moves on a number line. Its velocity at time $t$ ($t\ge0$) is $v(t)={v}$. How far does P travel from $t=0$ to $t={T}$? (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: Distance traveled is the integral of speed $|v(t)|$.
Split the interval at times when $v(t)=0$ and integrate according to the sign on each part.
ca1_totalDistVel.explanation: Velocity changes sign at ${zs}$ within the interval. Split at those times; the sign stays the same on each part, so add the absolute values of $\int v(t)\,dt$ to get ${parts}={ansf}.$

ca1_twoRootsK.prompt: For function $f(x)={f}$, what is the sum of all real values of $k$ for which equation $f(x)=k$ has exactly ${nr}$ distinct real roots? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Think about the boundary cases where the number of distinct roots changes: the horizontal line $y=k$ touches the graph at an extremum.
Use the graph shape to decide which extremum gives exactly ${nr}$ roots when the line is tangent.
ca1_twoRootsK.explanation: The extrema are ${ext}$. Compare the number of intersections when the horizontal line touches an extremum and when it does not. The values of $k$ that fit are ${kk}$, and their sum is ${ans}.$

ca1_velZeroAccel.prompt: A point P moves on a number line with position $x(t)={f}$ at time $t$ ($t\ge0$). What is its acceleration at the later of the two times when its velocity is 0? (Write numbers only.)
hints: Velocity is the derivative of position, $v(t)=x'(t)$; acceleration is the derivative of velocity, $a(t)=v'(t)$.
Find both roots of $v(t)=0$, then put the later root into $a(t)$.
ca1_velZeroAccel.explanation: $v(t)=x'(t)$, and the two roots of $v(t)=0$ are $t={t1}$ and $t={t2}$. At the later time $t={t2}$, $a(t)=v'(t)$ is ${ans}.$

ca2_addTheorem.prompt: Given ${ga}$, ${gb}$, ${ra}$, and ${rb}$, find the value of ${ask}$. (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: Use the given values and $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ to find the other needed trig values. The quadrant determines the sign.
Substitute the values into the addition formula.

ca2_areaCurves.prompt: The area enclosed by graphs $y={f}$, $y={g}$ and lines $x={a}$, $x={b}$ is $S$. Find ${ask}$. (Note: the x-axis is $y=0$.) (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)
hints: Integrate the equation of the lower graph subtracted from the upper graph over the interval.
Use $(\tan x)'=\frac{1}{\cos^{2}x}$ and $(\ln x)'=\frac{1}{x}$ to find antiderivatives of exponential, trig, and rational functions; use substitution for composite forms.
ca2_areaCurves.explanation: On interval $[{a},{b}]$, $y={f}$ is above, so $S=\int_{{a}}^{{b}}({f}-{gg})\,dx={wk}$. Therefore ${ask}={res}.$$$$$

ca2_ballDistance.prompt: A ball is dropped from height ${h}$ m. Each time it hits the ground, it bounces back to ${ratio} times the height of its previous fall, then falls again. This repeats forever. What is the total distance the ball travels, in meters? (Write a reduced fraction, or an integer if applicable. Example: 3/4)$
hints: Consider the first fall of ${h} m, then the later trips up and down (twice each bounce height).$
